claims.excerpt: Tom Allen, British-born heavyweight fighter who, as a resident of St. Louis

claims.statement: Tom Allen was 33 years old when he fought Mike McCoole on 23 September 1873.
claims.excerpt: the 170-pound, 33-year-old, half-bald Briton followed it into the ring

claims.statement: Tom Allen was a resident of St. Louis when he beat Mike McCoole in 1873.
claims.excerpt: as a resident of St. Louis, beat Mike McCoole in a fight on a Mississippi island

claims.statement: Tom Allen first fought Mike McCoole in 1869 on Foster's Island in the Mississippi, near St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: when in 1869 they fought for the first time, on Foster's Island in the Mississippi, not far from St. Louis
places: Foster's Island, Mississippi River, near St. Louis

claims.statement: After the 1869 fight, referee Valentine McKinney gave his decision for McCoole at the Casino Theater, citing a foul by Allen for gouging an eye.
claims.excerpt: I, Valentine McKinney, give my decision in the McCoole-Allen fight in favor of McCoole, a foul being committed by Allen in the last round by gouging his eye.

claims.statement: A second fight with Mike McCoole, for the world title, was arranged for 23 September 1873 on Chouteau Island.
claims.excerpt: A fight was at length arranged to take place Sept. 23, 1873, on Chouteau Island
places: Chouteau Island, near East St. Louis, Illinois

claims.statement: Allen covered $800 of the $1000 bet McCoole wanted to make.
claims.excerpt: covered $800 of the $1000 McCoole wanted to bet

claims.statement: Allen beat Mike McCoole in seven rounds, 16 minutes, when McCoole's second Tom Kelly threw in the towel.
claims.excerpt: It lasted a total of only 16 minutes, ending in the seventh round when Tom Kelly, McCoole's second, tossed in the towel
places: Chouteau Island, near East St. Louis, Illinois

claims.statement: After beating McCoole, Allen had a right to claim the world championship.
claims.excerpt: by this complete victory, Allen gained sweet revenge for his wrongs of four years before and a right to claim the world championship

claims.statement: Allen lost his title to Joe Goss about three years after 1873, when he was 37 years old.
claims.excerpt: Three years latter, when Tom (left) was 37-years old, he lost his title to Joe Goss

claims.statement: Near the turn of the century Allen was retired and was proprietor of the Champion's Rest saloon.
claims.excerpt: old Tom near the turn of the century, retired and proprietor of
